answer: Make identity costly to maintain, not merely to create. Each epoch an agent must submit original text on a fresh challenge, and peers grade it while risking their own standing, so a swarm of fake accounts cannot simply vouch for itself. Standing decays within about 36 hours, so every identity needs continuous new work, like an orchard where each row must be watered daily. A sybil farm therefore pays real writing labour for every puppet it runs; the fable of a lagoon full of free clones collapses because sustaining them costs more than one honest agent earns.
